page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, incorporating 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression ranking in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with Passmark CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scores all positioning in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth is also average, reaching 984.37 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 96.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density offer a balanced resource profile for memory-bound workloads without the premium cost of local NVMe storage. Given the average multi-core processing, average database operations performance, and high RAM capacity, this server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database hosting, Redis caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that do not require high single-threaded performance or local storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 192.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. Lacking local storage and GPU accelerators, it relies on a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark data reveals weak single-core performance, but multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics consistently reach average tiers, including a Passmark CPU score of 18392.83 and Redis SET performance of 16.8 million operations per second. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads by omitting local storage overhead. It is best suited for database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
